note: Corpus v0: vendored public repos only. Contrastive pairs and scenario configs are authored in S2, after the taxonomy exists.
attribution: How a consumer turns scan output into per-case findings. `scan_root` is the directory a scanner is pointed at; `path` is the file or directory the case is about. Each distinct `scan_root` is scanned exactly once per scanner, never once per case: the four Terraform cases share corpus/vendor/terragoat/terraform/aws, so scanning per case would report the same finding set four times over and inflate both the deduplication count and every per-category total. A finding is attributed to the case whose `path` the scanner's reported file matches - equal to that path, or under it by prefix when the path is a directory. A finding under a `scan_root` that matches no case `path` - that root holds 14 .tf files and only four are named by a case - takes the explicit state `unattributed`: it is counted and reported as such, never dropped and never folded into a default category. `category` is the label of the case a finding was attributed to, not a partition of resources: ec2.tf alone declares compute, networking and storage resources, so a single file's findings can belong to a case labelled with only one of the three.

terragoat.scope_note: AWS only. alicloud/azure/gcp/oracle omitted - they add rule volume, not category coverage.

cases.note: Reconciled against upstream at this pin: there is no vpc.tf. elb.tf is the only networking-only file (aws_elb, plain HTTP listener on lb_port 80). The rest of the networking footprint is split across ec2.tf (aws_vpc, aws_subnet x2, aws_internet_gateway, aws_route_table, aws_route, aws_route_table_association x2, aws_network_interface, aws_security_group, aws_flow_log) and db-app.tf (aws_security_group, aws_security_group_rule x2).

aws_instance, aws_ebs_volume, aws_ebs_snapshot, aws_volume_attachment. Upstream co-locates the VPC, subnet, route-table and security-group resources in this same file instead of a separate vpc.tf, and it also declares aws_s3_bucket 'flowbucket' as the flow-log target - so this file's 16 resource blocks span three of the five categories (compute, networking, storage). That is the concrete case for the top-level `attribution` rule's last clause: a category is a case label, not a partition of resources.

A directory, not a file: 24 files across 15 scenario directories. 16 are plain Kubernetes manifests (Deployment, Job, ClusterRole/RoleBinding, Kyverno policy); the other 8 are the metadata-db Helm chart. Measured across those 8 rather than assumed: Chart.yaml and values.yaml carry no Go template syntax and parse as plain YAML; 4 are templated YAML manifests a plain YAML parser cannot read (templates/deployment.yaml, templates/ingress.yaml, templates/service.yaml, templates/tests/test-connection.yaml); 2 are not YAML at all (templates/NOTES.txt, templates/_helpers.tpl). A skip list covering all 8 would silently drop two parseable files including the chart metadata. Helm is in conceptual scope but not the evaluation focus.

Hand-crafted. Three aws_iam_policy resources differing only in policy breadth. Corpus v0 cannot form a privilege pair: every genuine IAM policy type in it is single-instance (S2 design section 1). Measured on this pin: a single narrow S3 read action on a narrow resource ARN (the original draft) drew zero findings from all three scanners - a correctly-scoped policy is a true negative, not a defect - so narrow_scope grants sts:GetSessionToken instead, an action AWS itself only permits with Resource '*' (not a breadth choice, an IAM constraint), which checkov's credentials-exposure check (CKV_AWS_287) still flags once. Finding counts across the three resources are 1 (narrow), 2 (moderate), 10 (broad).

Hand-crafted. Corpus v0 has zero resource pairs sharing an identical issue-class set while differing in maximum severity, because severity co-varies with which rule fires (S2 design section 1). Verified on this pin: aws_ebs_volume.unencrypted_scratch (no `encrypted` attribute, mirroring TerraGoat's own web_host_storage) draws AVD-AWS-0027/AWS-0027 at LOW; aws_s3_bucket.no_cmk (no encryption block) draws AVD-AWS-0132/AWS-0132 at HIGH; both rules map to storage-key-management-cmk.
